results.title: Rioters loot stores, set fires in central Milan during cost-of-living protest
results.description: ROME (AP) — Rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday, emptying Piazza del Duomo and a luxury shopping arcade when the area would usually be teeming with shoppers. The march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. But masked protesters threw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and set fire to barricades made from bar tables. Images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car. Police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds. At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence in a social media post. “Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not,” she wrote, citing “hooligans who exploit demonstrations to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security and hold entire cities hostage.” Milan’s center-left mayor, Giuseppe Sala, said “the reasons for the protests were understandable. The violence against law enforcement and serious damage to the city are not justifiable.” The unrest coincided with nationwide demonstrations in neighboring France against rising living costs and in support of high school students’ grievances. French police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse violent protesters who joined the rallies.

results.title: Man drugged, robbed of over Ksh 575,000 and left for dead by notorious mchele ladies - They lured him into an Airbnb along Waiyaki Way after meeting in a club (PHOTOs)
results.description: Sunday, October 18, 2026 - Private investigator Jane Mugo has raised the alarm over two women she claims drugged her client, stole his mobile phones and withdrew KSh 575,000 from his bank account in a shocking incident reported at Kinoo Police Station. In a Facebook post, Mugo shared photographs of two women, one dressed in pink and the other in black, whom she accused of targeting unsuspecting men in bars and lodges using stupefying substances. According to the investigator, her client met the ladies in a club and bought them drinks and food. Mugo claimed that the women later advised the man to book an Airbnb along Waiyaki Way because he appeared tired and intoxicated. They reportedly told him to get some rest and drive the following day, not knowing that he was walking into a trap. The victim was drugged inside the Airbnb, robbed, and left for dead. The man only regained consciousness on Monday after reportedly being drugged from the early hours of Saturday. By then, KSh 575,000 had been withdrawn from his bank account through online transactions, while two mobile phones valued at approximately KSh 120,000 were also reported missing. Mugo claimed the women operate in areas including Kikuyu, Kinoo, Kabete, Regen, Kangemi and Nairobi, while warning members of the public to remain vigilant when socialising with strangers. The investigator said the matter had been reported at Kinoo Police Station and offered a KSh 100,000 reward to anyone who provides information leading to the arrest of the suspects. The Kenyan DAILY POST.

results.title: Leverage Edu to focus on AI, customer experience and new markets
results.description: Leverage Edu plans to increase its focus on artificial intelligence (AI), customer experience and marketing efficiency as it expands into new markets, founder Akshay Chaturvedi said. In a post on X following Entrackr’s report on the company’s FY26 financial numbers, Chaturvedi outlined priorities including technology adoption, university partnerships, cash flow management and new go-to-market (GTM) initiatives. He said expansion into less competitive international markets had helped the company enter new destinations. Better brand awareness and referrals had also reduced customer acquisition costs (CAC), although local players continued to hold an advantage in several regions. The company is expanding the use of AI across its operations. Chaturvedi said its AI suite, LE-AI, had started contributing to business functions. Leverage Edu has introduced AI-based analysis after counselling sessions to help coaches improve performance and is extending its use to consumers and partners. Chaturvedi also said higher uptake of financial services, housing, insurance and other offerings had improved customer lifetime value (LTV) and net promoter score (NPS). Leverage Edu’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25. Its net loss narrowed 82% to Rs 19.4 crore, while EBITDA turned positive at Rs 2 crore. International markets contributed Rs 297 crore, or over 81% of revenue, while domestic revenue grew 60% to Rs 67.4 crore. Founded in 2017, Leverage Edu helps students with overseas university admissions and education financing. It has raised nearly $90 million to date, including a $40 million Series C round led by Blume Ventures and DSG Consumer Partners in 2023.
